contribution: Methods for estimating demand and supply in differentiated-product markets, which created modern empirical industrial organization (the BLP framework and dynamic models of firm behavior)
rationale: This is a guess from memory, since the prize had not been announced as of today. The BLP random-coefficients demand model and Pakes's work on dynamic estimation are widely used in merger analysis, antitrust, trade, health and environmental economics. Empirical IO has not yet been recognized, which makes it a plausible pick, though many other fields are equally likely.
